# Castmorphic Subtitles

> A free Linux desktop app that downloads a YouTube video's subtitles in
> SRT, VTT, TXT, or Raw format. The video itself is never downloaded.

Castmorphic Subtitles is a single-window desktop app for Linux, shipped as
one AppImage. You paste a YouTube URL, it lists every subtitle language the
video has (manual and auto-generated, English first), you pick a language
and a format, and it saves the subtitle file.

Skipping the video download is hardcoded on and cannot be switched off, so
the video track is never requested from YouTube and nothing large is stored.

## Formats

- SRT: standard subtitle file with timestamps, works everywhere.
- VTT: WebVTT, the format most web video players expect natively.
- TXT: plain transcript, timestamps and formatting stripped out.
- Raw: whatever YouTube served, unconverted.

## Requirements

Linux, plus python3 version 3.10 or newer, which current Linux desktops
already ship. The window, the browser engine and the Python packages all
travel inside the AppImage. There is nothing to install, no Docker and no
account. It checks yt-dlp and its own version every time it starts.

## Licence and privacy

Free software. No account, no telemetry. The app talks to YouTube to fetch
subtitles and to GitHub to check for its own updates, and to nothing else.
